topicName: Garbage Collection Tuning, JVM Parameters, and Memory Leaks
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Garbage Collection Tuning, JVM Parameters, and Memory Leaks in Jenkins"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Jenkins is a Java-based automation server that frequently runs into performance bottlenecks due to memory management issues. As the number of jobs, build logs, and concurrent pipelines increases, the Java Virtual Machine (JVM) demands careful tuning to prevent OutOfMemoryError exceptions and excessive Garbage Collection (GC) pauses."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Jenkins JVM Memory Structure"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Jenkins JVM heap is primarily divided into the Young Generation (Eden space and Survivor spaces) and the Old Generation. Short-lived objects like step execution contexts are allocated in the Young Generation, while long-lived objects like plugin instances and job configurations migrate to the Old Generation."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Essential JVM Parameters for Production Jenkins"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"To configure Jenkins memory parameters, modify the initialization file specific to your operating system (e.g., /etc/default/jenkins on Ubuntu or jenkins.xml on Windows). Setting initial and maximum heap sizes to the same value prevents costly dynamic heap resizing."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"JAVA_ARGS=\"-Xms8g -Xmx8g -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200 -XX:+ParallelRefProcEnabled -XX:+ExplicitGCInvokesConcurrent\""},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-Xms8g and -Xmx8g: Sets the initial and maximum heap size to 8GB, avoiding heap fragmentation and resizing overhead."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-XX:+UseG1GC: Employs the Garbage-First collector, ideal for large heaps with predictable pause time requirements."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200: Sets a target for maximum GC pause time to maintain Jenkins UI responsiveness."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Identifying and Diagnosing Memory Leaks"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Memory leaks in Jenkins often stem from poorly written custom plugins, abandoned build histories, or excessive global variables. Symptoms include a steady climb in memory usage that never recedes after full GC cycles, ultimately resulting in a java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space."},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"When diagnosing a leak, capture a heap dump using the jmap utility or configure Jenkins to automatically generate a dump upon an OutOfMemoryError."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"jmap -dump:live,format=b0,file=/var/log/jenkins/heap_dump.hprof <jenkins_pid>"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Automated Heap Dump on OutOfMemoryError"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Add the following flags to your JAVA_ARGS to automatically capture a heap dump when a memory failure occurs, making post-mortem analysis with tools like Eclipse Memory Analyzer (MAT) straightforward."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"JAVA_ARGS=\"$JAVA_ARGS -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:HeapDumpPath=/var/log/jenkins/jenkins_oom.hprof\""},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Best Practices for Long-Term Jenkins Memory Health"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement retention policies: Limit the number of old build logs and artifacts kept on the master node."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Offload workloads: Use Jenkins agents (workers) to execute resource-intensive builds rather than running them on the master."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Audit plugins regularly: Outdated or abandoned plugins are primary sources of severe classloader and memory leaks."}]
